$comment: arb402 Orbit chain registry — copy to arb402.chains.json (or point
ARB402_CHAINS_FILE at it) to run the facilitator on any Arbitrum L3.
Entries are merged over the built-in chains by CAIP-2 id, so you can also
use this file to override a built-in — e.g. to give Arbitrum Nova the
EIP-3009 token you deployed, or to pin a private RPC for Arbitrum One.
Run 'arb402 chains --verify' after editing: it probes each token on-chain
for EIP-3009 support and checks that the declared EIP-712 domain matches
the contract's own DOMAIN_SEPARATOR.

chains.$comment: A typical Orbit L3 with its own EIP-3009 USDC deployment.
chains.name: My Orbit Chain

$comment: Must implement EIP-3009 (transferWithAuthorization). 'name' and
'version' are the token's EIP-712 domain values, NOT cosmetic — if
they disagree with the contract, every signature recovers to the
wrong address and settlement fails with no on-chain explanation.
Default to Circle's ('USD Coin', '2') only if you deployed Circle's
implementation.
token.name: USD Coin

$comment: Overriding a built-in: Arbitrum Nova's bridged USDC.e is a plain
gateway ERC-20 with no EIP-3009, so arb402 ships Nova with no default
token. Uncomment and point this at an EIP-3009-capable token to
enable settlement on Nova.
"token": {
"address": "0xYourEip3009TokenOnNova",
"name": "USD Coin",
"version": "2",
"decimals": 6
chains.name: Arbitrum Nova
